evidence: Petr. 44: prō lutō erat annōna (Lewis & Short s.v. lutum)

phrases.latin: «Bene ēmistī,» inquit avus. «Hōc annī tempore vīlia sunt māla.»
phrases.english: “That’s a bargain,” said Grandpa. “Apples are cheap at this time of year.”

phrases.latin: Hic pānis vīlis est; duōs emāmus.
phrases.english: This bread is cheap; let’s buy two.

phrases.latin: vēnit vīlissima rērum hīc aqua, sed pānis longē pulcherrimus …
phrases.english: here water, the cheapest of things, is sold, but the bread is by far the finest …

sources: Lewis & Short: vilis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 96, 130, 289, 304, 332.
